title: Leading Yourself Before You Lead Anyone Else
subtitle: The disciplines of self leadership for pastors, why the inner life governs the public ministry, and how a leader who cannot govern his own soul will eventually wreck the people he leads.

sections.title: The First Person You Lead Is the Hardest
sections.body:
We give our lives to leading other people. We study how to motivate them, shepherd them, organize them, move them toward a vision. And we quietly assume that the man doing the leading is already handled.

He is not. The hardest person any leader will ever lead is himself. The appetites do not retire when you are ordained. The laziness, the anger, the wandering eye, the love of comfort, the need to be admired, all of it follows you into the office and waits. A man can lead a church of a thousand and not be able to lead himself across the room away from the thing that is killing him.

You cannot give what you do not govern. The field you tend first is your own soul, or you have no business in anyone else's.

sections.title: What You Do When No One Is Watching Is the Real You
sections.body:
Self leadership is built in private. It is the prayer you pray when no one will know whether you prayed. It is the Bible read for your soul and not your sermon. It is the body you keep, the sleep you protect, the food you do not abuse, the rest you take on purpose because you are a creature and not a machine.

These are not the small matters before the real work. They are the real work. The public ministry is downstream of the private disciplines, always. A spring cannot give clean water from a poisoned source, no matter how good the plumbing is on the surface.

The disciplines are not how you earn God's love. They are how you stay near the One whose love you already have, so that what flows out of you is Him and not merely your effort.

sections.title: Rule the Appetites or Be Ruled by Them
sections.body:
Paul said he disciplined his body and kept it under control, lest after preaching to others he himself should be disqualified. He was not being dramatic. He had watched gifted men fall, and he knew that gifting does not protect a man from his own appetites. It only raises the stakes when they win.

The leader who will not say no to himself in small things has no power to say no in large ones. The man who cannot leave the phone alone, who cannot resist the second helping of comfort, who cannot govern his temper at home, is training himself to lose the bigger battles before they arrive. Self control is a muscle, and it is built in the unseen daily reps long before the test comes.

What you indulge in private, you empower. What you discipline in private, you are free from in public.

sections.title: Know What Is Happening Inside You
sections.body:
Many leaders are strangers to their own hearts. They feel the anger but never ask where it came from. They feel the dread on Sunday morning and never trace it to its root. They are skilled at reading rooms and blind to reading themselves, and the unexamined interior leaks out as moodiness, control, and harm to the people closest to them.

Self leadership means paying attention to what is going on under the surface. Why am I anxious. What is this resentment about. What am I afraid of that I am calling conviction. The leader who refuses this work does not become emotionally simple. He becomes emotionally dangerous, because the things he will not face in himself he will inflict on others.

Know yourself. Not as an end, but so that you can bring the real man, and not a managed image, before God to be healed.

sections.title: You Will Lead Others Exactly as Well as You Lead Yourself
sections.body:
There is a ceiling on every ministry, and the ceiling is the leader's own soul. The church will not grow past the man's character for long. The cracks he ignores in himself become the cracks that bring the whole thing down, usually years later, usually in public, usually after everyone said he seemed so strong.

So do the unseen work. Govern the appetites. Keep the disciplines. Examine the heart. Lead the one man God has given you total responsibility for before you presume to lead anyone else.

Not a leader who has it all together. A leader honest enough to lead himself toward the One who does.
